decisions.descriptionMarkdown: Two homes, split by language and by whether a thing is a crate. `crates/` holds every Rust crate: the libraries consumers depend on, plus the never-shipped verification crates named `gpux_tests_*` so they sort together (`gpux_tests_benchmark`, `gpux_tests_conformance`). `tools/` holds what drives or hosts the tests: `testkit` (runner), `perf` (Zed's `#[perf]` timer), `browser` (Playwright), `android` and `ios` (app shells). Pass/fail UI tests and numbers-only benchmarks stay distinct by crate: `gpux_tests_conformance` is run by `gpux-testkit lane ...` in CI, `gpux_tests_benchmark` by `run.py` locally for the improvement loops.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- Lanes, scenes, specs and benchmark scenarios keep their content; only locations and names change.
- Unit tests and `#[gpux::bench]` suites stay beside the crates they exercise.
- No Zed crate folder under `crates/` is renamed or moved.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: The owner rejected tests in three places plus two tool roots (`tooling/`, `tools-node/`) and asked for one predictable place per kind, with UI tests and improvement-loop benchmarks distinguishable. Keeping the Rust crates in `crates/` (owner's choice over `tools/tests/`) keeps one rule for where a crate lives; the `gpux_tests_` prefix gives the grouping and the suffix the distinction.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: Rename the conformance crate in folder, package and library together: `crates/gpux_tests_conformance`, package `gpux-tests-conformance`, `[lib] name = "gpux_tests_conformance"`, workspace key `gpux_tests_conformance`. Every folder in `crates/` matches its library's Rust name, and this crate is gpux's own (no Zed provenance), so the rename follows the convention instead of creating its only exception. Consumers change their `use gpux_conformance::...` to `gpux_tests_conformance::...` (about 80 references in about 50 files: the crate's own tests and examples, the testkit's sources and tests). The testkit's cargo selectors (`-p gpux-conformance`) and its workspace-root probe (`crates/gpux_conformance/Cargo.toml`) change with it; the probe keeps requiring the root `Cargo.toml` too.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- The crate keeps its features (`test-host`, `app-host`, `diagnostics`), examples, `exclude = ["tests/goldens/**"]`, description and keywords.
- The goldens' location relative to the crate is unchanged, so lane C finds them through `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` as before.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: Not published yet (crates.io has no `gpux-conformance`, 2026-10-16), so the package rename is free now and would orphan a crate after the first release. Keeping the old library name under a new folder would break the folder-equals-library-name convention that every other crate follows.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: Identifiers that travel at runtime between the hosts, the testkit, Playwright and the devices are a protocol, not a package name, and stay unchanged: `report::MARKER` (`gpux-conformance:`), the hosts' `gpux-conformance-host:` marker, `globalThis.__gpuxConformance`, `dev.gpux.conformance` (Android package, iOS bundle id), `ios::SIMULATOR_NAME`, the APK file name and `GpuxConformance` (XcodeGen project name).
decisions.invariantsMarkdown: - Recorded fixtures (`tests/fixtures/android_logcat.txt`, `desktop_host_stdout.txt`, Playwright listings) are not edited by this epic.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: Renaming them would touch the Playwright fixtures, the Java helpers' expectations, installed Simulator devices and CI caches for no layout benefit, and would make the guard's package-name scan ambiguous.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: Move `tooling/{testkit,perf,android,ios}` to `tools/{testkit,perf,android,ios}` with `git mv`; update the root workspace `members` and the `perf` workspace dependency path; keep both package names. The testkit's inline path joins become small named functions beside the existing `ios::project` so the new group can assert them: `android::manifest(root)` (`tools/android/AndroidManifest.xml`), `ios::spec(root)` and `ios::project(root)` (`tools/ios/...`). `lane_coverage.rs`'s relative path to the conformance tests becomes `../../crates/gpux_tests_conformance/tests` (the depth from `tools/testkit` is the same as from `tooling/testkit`).
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- `.cargo/config.toml`'s `perf-test`/`perf-compare` aliases select `-p gpux-perf` and need no change.
- The generated `GpuxConformance.xcodeproj` stays git-ignored by the existing `*.xcodeproj` rule.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: Move the tracked files of `tools-node/` to `tools/browser/` with `git mv` (git-ignored `node_modules/` and reports stay behind and are reinstalled with `pnpm install` there). `WebPaths::tools_node` becomes `WebPaths::browser` (`root/tools/browser`), and the testkit's Playwright messages and its local-GPU prerequisite text name `tools/browser`. Inside the project the two relative paths gain one level: `playwright.config.ts` writes to `../../artifacts-temp/testkit/b`, and `fixtures/catalog.ts`'s default dist is `fixtures/../../../target/gpux-web/dist`. `GPUX_DIST`, which the testkit passes, keeps precedence.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown: - Spec files, tags, profiles and the committed `pnpm-lock.yaml` are unchanged.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: Move `benchmark/` to `crates/gpux_tests_benchmark/` with `git mv` and rename package and library to `gpux-tests-benchmark` / `gpux_tests_benchmark` (binary `gpux-bench` unchanged). It stays a standalone workspace: its own `[workspace]` table, its own git-ignored `Cargo.lock` and `target*` folders, version `0.0.0`, never a root workspace member. Path dependencies become `../<crate>`. `run.py`: `ROOT = BENCH.parent.parent`; `Tree.dirty()` adds the pathspec `:(exclude)crates/gpux_tests_benchmark` so scenario edits and results never count as a dirty gpux tree; artifact names follow the library (`libgpux_tests_benchmark.a`, `gpux_tests_benchmark.wasm`, `./gpux_tests_benchmark.js` in `web/index.html`); `web/run.mjs` resolves Playwright through `../../../tools/browser/package.json`. The internal shape (shared `src/scenarios/`, one entry point per target, `ios/`, `web/`, `results/`) is unchanged.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- Root `cargo` commands, CI and `cargo package --workspace` never build it.
- `results/`, `RESULTS.md` and `LOOP-*.md` move with it unchanged (historical records).
- No native/wasm folder split: the scenarios have no target-specific variants.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: The packaging rule "keep every crate publishable" was written for workspace crates; the benchmark was deliberately kept out of the workspace so its WASM and iOS dependencies never enter the root lock file or CI. Living under `crates/` beside the conformance crate is the owner's choice; the rule text gains the explicit exemption (DOCS-4) rather than the benchmark becoming a publishable member.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: Update every live reference in one pass after the moves: CI workflows, `README.md`, `docs/` except the historical folders, `LINUX-WSL.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` (both carry the Crate Layout section), the gpux skill (`.claude/skills/gpux/**`, including the preserve list in `update-from-zed-gpui-closure.md`), the benchmark README, and source comments. Add `tools/README.md` as the map (folder, what it is, the command that runs it). Sync memory narrowly: the three affected `rules.md` files, the `state.md` backlinks that point at moved paths, and the path mentions inside the current decisions on gpux-testkit, the test lanes and lanes B, E and F (path facts only; the decisions themselves stand). After the epic, promote one new decision record, `repository/validation/<date>-repository-validation-test-tooling-layout.md`, that builds on those decisions.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- Historical records keep their paths: `.agentx/tasks/**`, `.agentx/experiments/**`, `docs/changelog/**`, `docs/history/**`, `docs/measurements/**`, `ToFix/**`, the benchmark's `RESULTS.md`, `LOOP-*.md`, `results/**`.
- `.agentx/memory/decisions/INDEX.md` gains the promoted record only at promotion.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: A testkit integration test group, `tools/testkit/tests/repository_layout.rs`, reads the checkout from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../..` and the tracked file list from `git ls-files` (no new dependency: plain string matching, as the other testkit tests do). Scanned files: tracked text files except the historical records of d-references, `tools/testkit/tests/fixtures/**`, `vendor/**`, `Cargo.lock` and the guard file itself. Patterns: `tooling/` and root-level `benchmark/` match only when not preceded by an ASCII letter, digit, `_` or `/` (so RayX's memory domain `knowledge/tooling/` and `crates/gpux_tests_benchmark/` never match); `tools-node`, `crates/gpux_conformance` and the identifier `gpux_conformance` match anywhere; `gpux-conformance` matches only after `-p `, `--exclude `, `package = "` or `name = "` (the runtime markers of d-protocol-ids stay legal). Failures list `file:line: pattern`. Each scan has a seeded-failure test on a temporary file so it can fail.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown: - The guard needs a git checkout; outside one it fails with a message saying so, never passes vacuously.
